stem: A hotel group wants two agents: (1) a public web chat that takes room bookings through a strict sequence of steps with validation and payment handoff, and (2) an internal assistant that lets revenue managers ask ad-hoc questions over Drive spreadsheets and Gmail. Which tool choices fit? (Choose two.)

options.A: Agent Designer in Gemini Enterprise for the internal assistant
options.B: Agent Designer for the public booking chat, because it supports conditional routing
options.C: One ADK agent for both use cases, deployed to Cloud Run
options.D: CX Agent Studio for the booking chat, with a flow for the strict sequence
options.E: CX Agent Studio for the internal assistant, because it has data store tools

rationale.A: Agent Designer builds internal no-code agents connected to Google and third-party data sources.
rationale.B: Agent Designer serves Gemini Enterprise users inside the organisation, not public customer channels.
rationale.C: The requirement is low-code; ADK means a code project for both teams.
rationale.D: Customer-facing conversational agents with deterministic sub-procedures are CX Agent Studio's target.
rationale.E: Possible but misplaced: employees already work in Gemini Enterprise with Workspace connectors.

stem: A team asks a coding agent to refactor a 12-year-old billing module that has almost no tests. The refactor must not change behaviour, and reviewers cannot read a 9,000-line diff. What should the engineering lead require?

options.A: Characterisation tests of current behaviour first, then small reviewed refactor steps
options.B: Asking the agent to confirm in its final message that behaviour did not change
options.C: Rewriting the module from scratch in a new language so the old behaviour is irrelevant
options.D: One large refactor PR that the agent explains in a detailed summary for reviewers

rationale.A: Pinning existing behaviour with tests and landing incremental changes is what makes agent refactors verifiable and reviewable.
rationale.B: Self-assessment by the agent is not evidence.
rationale.C: Changes behaviour by design and multiplies risk.
rationale.D: An explanation is not verification, and a huge diff defeats review.

stem: An organisation wants a documented process before any new tool is exposed to production agents: security review, an owner, and registration so policy can be applied. A team objects that this slows delivery. What is the best compromise?

options.A: Allow any tool in production and review after the first incident
options.B: Require full architecture review for every tool regardless of risk
options.C: Lightweight review with registration, fast-tracked for read-only
options.D: Let each team self-certify without central registration

rationale.A: Accepts unbounded risk as the default.
rationale.B: The friction the team objects to, with little added safety for read-only tools.
rationale.C: Risk-proportionate review keeps the governance requirement while removing friction for low-risk, read-only capabilities.
rationale.D: Leaves no inventory and no way to apply policy.

stem: A claims workflow must branch: simple claims are auto-approved, medium claims go to a review agent, and high-value claims go to a human and then back into the workflow if approved. The team wants the routing logic explicit and testable rather than emergent from a prompt. Which design fits best?

options.A: A ParallelAgent that runs all three paths and discards the irrelevant results
options.B: One LlmAgent with instructions describing the three paths and when to use each
options.C: A SequentialAgent with all three handlers in order and early returns in prompts
options.D: A graph workflow with conditional edges and a human-input node that resumes

rationale.A: Wasteful and would auto-approve claims that need review.
rationale.B: Makes routing emergent and hard to test, the opposite of the requirement.
rationale.C: Sequential templates cannot express branching or a resumable pause.
rationale.D: Graph workflows express conditional routing and resumable human input explicitly, keeping control flow testable.

stem: An architect must evaluate Google, partner and open models side by side before selecting one for a new agent, and wants a single place in Google Cloud to discover and try them. Where should they start?

options.A: Agent Registry, which lists every model available to agents in the organisation
options.B: Skill Registry, whose skills each wrap one foundation model for comparison
options.C: Model Garden, the catalogue of foundation models from Google, partners and open source
options.D: Agent Garden, the managed endpoint that serves every model on demand

rationale.A: Agent Registry catalogs agents, tools, skills and MCP servers, not foundation models.
rationale.B: Skill Registry stores agent skills, not models.
rationale.C: Model Garden is described as a library of 200+ foundation models from Google, partners and open source for discovery and experimentation.
rationale.D: Agent Garden provides samples; it is not a model catalogue or serving endpoint.

stem: A developer finished an ADK agent locally and asks which deploy targets the ADK CLI offers out of the box. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only Cloud Run, with Agent Runtime reserved for no-code agents
options.B: App Engine standard and Cloud Functions
options.C: Docker, Cloud Run and Agent Runtime via the ADK CLI
options.D: Only Agent Runtime, since ADK agents cannot run in containers

rationale.A: Agent Runtime is a first-class ADK deployment target.
rationale.B: Not the documented ADK deploy targets.
rationale.C: adk deploy supports docker, cloud_run and agent_engine targets, with options such as --with_ui.
rationale.D: ADK supports container and Cloud Run deployment too.

stem: A law firm created an Agent Search data store over its document management exports in Cloud Storage and connected it to Gemini Enterprise. During UAT, a junior associate retrieves summaries of partner-only files. The team now wants document-level permissions enforced for all users. What must they do?

options.A: Move partner-only files to a separate bucket and remove the associate's IAM access to it
options.B: Create a new access-controlled data store and re-ingest with ACL metadata
options.C: Turn on access control for the existing data store and re-import the documents with ACL metadata
options.D: Add an instruction telling the agent never to reveal documents marked partner-only

rationale.A: Bucket IAM does not govern what the search app returns to end users; ACLs on the data store do.
rationale.B: Access control must be selected at data store creation and cannot be turned on for an existing data store; documents carry acl_info readers.
rationale.C: The setting cannot be turned on or off for an existing data store.
rationale.D: Prompt instructions are not access control and are easily bypassed.

stem: A user told a travel agent in March 'I live in Lisbon' and in August 'I just moved to Porto'. With Memory Bank, the team sees a single up-to-date memory about the user's city rather than two conflicting facts. Which capability explains this?

options.A: Similarity search returns only the most recent of any two similar memories
options.B: Consolidation merges new facts with existing memories, keeping revisions of the change
options.C: The session service overwrote the March session when the August one was created
options.D: TTL expiry deleted the March memory automatically after 90 days

rationale.A: Retrieval ranks memories; it does not merge or update them.
rationale.B: Memory Bank performs memory consolidation to merge newly extracted information with existing memories and maintains memory revisions.
rationale.C: Sessions are separate conversations; memories are consolidated in Memory Bank.
rationale.D: TTL removes stale memories by time, not by contradiction, and none was configured here.

stem: A team runs one agent on Agent Runtime and another in a container on Cloud Run, and wants both to use Agent Identity rather than shared service accounts. Is that supported?

options.A: Yes: Agent Identity supports Agent Runtime, Gemini Enterprise and Cloud Run
options.B: No: Agent Identity is only available for agents deployed to Agent Runtime
options.C: Only with Anthos Service Mesh issuing the certificates
options.D: Only if the Cloud Run agent is rewritten with ADK

rationale.A: The documentation lists Agent Runtime, Gemini Enterprise and Cloud Run as supported runtimes for Agent Identity.
rationale.B: Cloud Run and Gemini Enterprise are listed as supported.
rationale.C: Certificates are auto-provisioned by the platform.
rationale.D: Framework choice is not the gating factor.

stem: A security engineer asks what happens to user requests if Model Armor cannot be reached while screening is configured. What should you tell them, and what should follow?

options.A: Requests are queued and screened retroactively when it recovers
options.B: All requests are blocked until Model Armor recovers, so plan for downtime
options.C: The request proceeds unscreened, so add alerting on screening failures
options.D: The agent automatically switches to a local filter model

rationale.A: There is no retroactive screening queue.
rationale.B: Screening failures do not block traffic by default.
rationale.C: If Model Armor is unreachable the request continues without screening, so teams need monitoring to detect the gap.
rationale.D: No such fallback exists.

stem: A B2B SaaS company runs two different agents (billing and onboarding) for thousands of users. Each agent must only retrieve memories created for the same user by that same agent. How should memories be scoped?

options.A: Scope memories by both the user and the agent name
options.B: Use one global scope and add the user ID as a tag in each memory's text
options.C: Create a separate Google Cloud project for each user's memories
options.D: Scope memories by user only and filter by agent in the prompt

rationale.A: Memory Bank isolates collections of memories by identity scope, including agent_name and user fields.
rationale.B: No isolation; one user's memories could surface for another.
rationale.C: Operationally absurd at thousands of users; scopes provide isolation.
rationale.D: Retrieves the other agent's memories and relies on the model to ignore them.

stem: A platform team needs one policy that allows an agent group to reach an internal API only when the request targets a specific resource path, and denies everything else for that group. How are such rules expressed in IAM access policies?

options.A: As a list of allowed URLs in the gateway's YAML configuration file
options.B: As natural-language sentences evaluated by a model at request time
options.C: As rules with allow or deny effects and CEL-based conditions on the destination
options.D: As firewall rules attached to the destination's subnet

rationale.A: Policy is expressed as IAM access policy rules, not gateway URL lists.
rationale.B: That describes semantic governance, not identity-based access policies.
rationale.C: Each rule in an access policy contains an effect and CEL-based conditions specifying destination resources and access criteria.
rationale.D: Network rules cannot express resource-path conditions for API calls.

stem: After wiring Model Armor into Agent Gateway, screening silently does not happen. Which IAM configuration should you verify?

options.A: The gateway's Model Armor callout user and user roles
options.B: That each agent identity has the Model Armor admin role
options.C: That the project's default service account has Owner
options.D: That end users hold the Model Armor viewer role

rationale.A: The Agent Gateway integration requires roles/modelarmor.calloutUser and modelarmor.user.
rationale.B: Agents do not call Model Armor directly in this integration.
rationale.C: Owner is never the right answer for a missing specific role.
rationale.D: End users are not the calling principal.

stem: A remote A2A agent finishes a task and must return a generated PDF plus a short text explanation to the calling agent. Which A2A elements carry these?

options.A: Artifacts for the generated outputs, with Parts holding the file and text
options.B: A Message with role assistant carrying the PDF as base64 in its text field
options.C: The Agent Card, updated with a link to the generated file
options.D: A Task object whose ID resolves to the file in a shared bucket

rationale.A: Artifacts are tangible outputs generated during a task, and Parts are the content containers used within messages and artifacts.
rationale.B: Messages carry conversational turns; generated outputs are artifacts.
rationale.C: Agent Cards are discovery documents, not result carriers.
rationale.D: Tasks track work state; outputs are returned as artifacts.

stem: A 400-engineer organisation keeps rebuilding the same capabilities because teams cannot find existing agents, skills and MCP tools. Leadership wants one catalog to discover and reuse them, with governance applied centrally. What should they adopt?

options.A: Example Store, which holds reusable agent examples for discovery
options.B: Model Garden, extended with the organisation's internal agents
options.C: Agent Registry as the central catalog
options.D: A Confluence page per team listing their agents and tools

rationale.A: Example Store serves few-shot examples at run time.
rationale.B: Model Garden catalogs foundation models.
rationale.C: Agent Registry is a centralized catalog to store, discover and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills and agents.
rationale.D: Documentation drifts and provides no governance or programmatic discovery.

stem: An organisation wants employees to ask questions across Drive, SharePoint and Jira with per-user permissions honoured, and does not want to build a retrieval pipeline. A developer proposes writing a custom RAG Engine corpus over exports of these systems. What is the better choice and why?

options.A: Agent Retrieval, because collections enforce per-user access automatically
options.B: A BigQuery export with row-level security applied to each document
options.C: Agent Search with connectors, because it preserves per-user document permissions
options.D: RAG Engine, because it is the only service that supports third-party sources

rationale.A: Agent Retrieval is a vector store; it does not implement enterprise document ACLs.
rationale.B: Rebuilds search and permissions from scratch for a solved problem.
rationale.C: Agent Search data stores carry ACLs and use the identity provider to filter results per user, which exports into a custom corpus would lose.
rationale.D: Agent Search connectors cover third-party sources including SharePoint and Jira.

stem: A grounded agent occasionally states product limits that do not appear in any retrieved document. A colleague proposes enabling Model Armor to stop it. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: Model Armor screens injection and safety, not grounding
options.B: Correct, provided inspect-and-block mode is enabled for responses
options.C: Correct: enabling the Sensitive Data Protection filter removes invented details
options.D: Correct: Model Armor's responsible-AI filters block unsupported claims

rationale.A: Model Armor's filters target prompt injection, responsible-AI categories, sensitive data and malicious URLs, not whether a claim is supported by context.
rationale.B: Enforcement mode does not give Model Armor a grounding capability.
rationale.C: SDP detects sensitive data, not fabrication.
rationale.D: Those filters cover harmful content categories, not factuality.

stem: Sales managers want a Gemini Enterprise assistant they can ask free-form questions about pipeline health, with follow-up questions that depend on earlier answers. The path through the conversation is different every time. Which Agent Designer option fits?

options.A: A scheduled workflow that emails a pipeline report
options.B: A chat agent
options.C: A CX Agent Studio flow with a page per report
options.D: A workflow with a conditional route for each anticipated question

rationale.A: Useful, but it does not support interactive follow-up questions.
rationale.B: Agent Designer describes chat agents as conversational and primarily non-deterministic, suited to dynamic tasks driven by the user.
rationale.C: State machines fit scripted customer journeys, not open-ended analysis.
rationale.D: Workflows suit defined sequences; enumerating free-form questions is impractical.

stem: An agent completes tasks correctly but calls several unnecessary tools on the way, raising cost. The team wants a number that reflects how many of its calls were actually relevant. Which metric fits?

options.A: trajectory_precision, which measures how many predicted calls were relevant
options.B: trajectory_in_order_match, which returns 0 when extra calls appear
options.C: trajectory_single_tool_use, which checks that only one tool was used
options.D: trajectory_exact_match, which penalises every deviation equally

rationale.A: trajectory_precision measures how many of the predicted trajectory's tool calls are relevant according to the reference, returning a value between 0 and 1.
rationale.B: It tolerates extra calls and returns a binary result.
rationale.C: It checks whether a specified tool was used, not overall relevance.
rationale.D: Binary and blunt; it cannot quantify how many calls were unnecessary.

stem: A RAG agent sends 18 retrieved chunks of 1,500 tokens each into every request, and cost is dominated by input tokens. Evaluation shows answer quality is unchanged when only the top 5 chunks are used. What should the team do?

options.A: Cache the 18 chunks per query string for an hour
options.B: Summarise each chunk with a second model call before the main call
options.C: Retrieve broadly but rerank and pass only the top chunks to the model
options.D: Keep all 18 chunks but switch to a cheaper model to halve the price

rationale.A: Caching identical queries does not reduce per-request context.
rationale.B: Adds calls and latency to fix a problem reranking solves.
rationale.C: Reranking lets the system keep recall while cutting the tokens sent to the model, with quality verified by evaluation.
rationale.D: Reduces quality while still paying for unnecessary context.

stem: A team logs full prompts and responses for debugging, including customer messages that contain payment details. Compliance objects. Which change preserves debuggability with the least data risk?

options.A: Stop logging prompts and responses entirely
options.B: Shorten log retention to seven days and keep full content
options.C: Keep full logs but restrict access to the security team
options.D: Redact sensitive fields, keeping correlation identifiers

rationale.A: Removes the ability to debug agent behaviour.
rationale.B: Reduces the window but not the exposure.
rationale.C: Sensitive data is still retained broadly and remains a breach risk.
rationale.D: Redaction with identifiers keeps traces useful for debugging while removing the sensitive content from logs.

stem: A team has no ML engineers and wants to avoid running an embedding pipeline, but still needs semantic search over new documents as they arrive in their retrieval collection. Which Agent Retrieval capability helps?

options.A: Autogenerated embeddings from built-in models
options.B: Scheduled exports to Feature Store that generate vectors nightly
options.C: Bring your own embeddings, which is the only supported option
options.D: Automatic chunking of documents into sentences before storage

rationale.A: Agent Retrieval can automatically populate embedding fields using built-in models, and also supports bring-your-own embeddings.
rationale.B: Not how embeddings are produced for a collection, and it is not near-real-time.
rationale.C: BYOE is supported but not the only option.
rationale.D: Chunking strategy is not the described feature.

stem: An ADK operations agent can call `restart_production_service`. The SRE lead wants the agent to pause and obtain an explicit yes/no from the on-call engineer through the chat UI before the tool runs, and resume afterwards, with no custom approval service. What should you use?

options.A: A Cloud Tasks queue that delays each restart by ten minutes
options.B: A before_model_callback that blocks all model calls containing the word restart
options.C: Tool confirmation: require_confirmation on the FunctionTool, which pauses for a yes/no
options.D: An instruction telling the agent to ask the engineer before calling the restart tool

rationale.A: Delay is not approval, and adds the custom service the lead wanted to avoid.
rationale.B: Blocks rather than asks, and does not resume after approval.
rationale.C: ADK tool confirmation lets a FunctionTool pause execution for a yes/no confirmation; ADK emits a confirmation request event to the client.
rationale.D: Advisory; the model can call the tool without asking.

stem: A pharmaceutical company's Gemini Enterprise agent answers questions about standard operating procedures. Auditors require every answer to be traceable to the specific SOP version it came from. Which configuration best supports this?

options.A: Ground on a versioned SOP data store and require citations
options.B: Log every answer to BigQuery for auditors to review later
options.C: Paste the current SOPs into the agent instructions each month
options.D: Let the model answer from general pharmaceutical knowledge

rationale.A: Grounding on an enterprise data store with metadata and citations makes answers traceable to sources.
rationale.B: Logging records answers but does not tie them to source documents.
rationale.C: No per-answer traceability, context limits, and stale content between updates.
rationale.D: Not the company's procedures and not traceable.

stem: A security team allows the Antigravity CLI on developer laptops only if shell commands the agent runs cannot modify files outside the project or make unexpected outbound network calls. They do not want the startup cost of a VM or container per command. What should developers enable?

options.A: A subagent with a restricted tools list that runs all shell commands
options.B: The always-proceed permission mode together with a strict AGENTS.md rules file
options.C: The terminal sandbox (enableTerminalSandbox), which uses OS-native isolation
options.D: A Docker container per command, configured through a pre-tool hook

rationale.A: Tool restrictions limit which tools exist, not what an allowed shell command can touch.
rationale.B: Always-proceed removes review, and rules do not technically contain commands.
rationale.C: The terminal sandbox uses nsjail, sandbox-exec or AppContainer to contain file writes and network access with no VM or container overhead; it is off by default.
rationale.D: Exactly the per-command container overhead the team wanted to avoid.

stem: A team deployed an ADK agent to Agent Runtime and sees logs but no traces in the console's Traces tab. They expected step-by-step spans. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Traces appear only after 10,000 requests have been recorded
options.B: ADK agents cannot be traced; only custom frameworks emit spans
options.C: Telemetry was not enabled at deploy time for the AdkApp
options.D: Cloud Trace must be replaced by a self-hosted Jaeger backend for agents

rationale.A: There is no such threshold.
rationale.B: ADK applications can be instrumented with OpenTelemetry.
rationale.C: Tracing requires enabling OpenTelemetry for the deployed app, for example the telemetry environment variable set when deploying to Agent Runtime.
rationale.D: Agent traces are exported to Google Cloud Observability.

stem: An internal agent is used heavily between 09:00 and 11:00 and almost never at night. The team pays for provisioned capacity around the clock on their current platform, and cold starts during the morning peak are hurting first-response latency. What is the best approach?

options.A: Schedule a nightly batch job to pre-compute the morning's answers
options.B: Scale purely on demand with no warm instances and accept cold starts
options.C: Keep capacity provisioned for peak at all times to guarantee latency
options.D: Serverless scaling with a small warm floor sized for the morning ramp

rationale.A: Agent conversations cannot be pre-computed.
rationale.B: Leaves the morning latency problem unsolved.
rationale.C: Pays for idle capacity for most of the day, which is the current complaint.
rationale.D: Scale-to-zero removes idle cost while a minimal warm pool absorbs cold starts during the known peak.

stem: An LLM-judged criterion gives slightly different verdicts on re-runs of the same case, making CI flaky. Which property of final_response_match_v2 helps, and what else should the team do?

options.A: It falls back to response_match_score when the judge is uncertain
options.B: It runs the judge at temperature zero, which removes all variance
options.C: It caches judgements per case, so the first verdict is reused forever
options.D: It majority-votes several judge samples; keep cases decisive

rationale.A: No such fallback is described.
rationale.B: Determinism is not guaranteed and is not how the criterion is described.
rationale.C: Caching verdicts would hide genuine regressions.
rationale.D: final_response_match_v2 uses multiple sampling with a majority vote, configurable by judge model and sample count, and unambiguous cases reduce residual variance.

stem: Developers use Claude Code and Cursor on laptops to call internal agents and MCP tools hosted on Agent Runtime. The security team wants those client connections authenticated, authorised by policy and observable centrally. Which Agent Gateway mode applies?

options.A: Gemini Enterprise's gateway integration, which covers developer IDE traffic
options.B: Client-to-Agent (ingress) mode for clients calling agents
options.C: Agent-to-Anywhere (egress) mode, which governs any traffic that touches an agent
options.D: No gateway: coding agents connect directly with personal service-account keys

rationale.A: Gemini Enterprise does not support Client-to-Agent mode.
rationale.B: Client-to-Agent secures communications between clients such as Cursor, Claude Code or Gemini CLI and agents or tools running on Google Cloud.
rationale.C: Egress governs agents on Google Cloud calling out to servers and APIs anywhere.
rationale.D: Loses central policy and observability and spreads long-lived keys.

stem: During an incident, an on-call engineer needs to see the exact sequence of model and tool calls for one slow user session, including inputs and outputs per step. Which view should they open?

options.A: The Logs tab, filtered to the session's severity levels
options.B: The Usage dashboard, filtered to the session's tokens
options.C: The evaluation results for the most recent run
options.D: The agent's Traces tab, showing spans for that session as a graph

rationale.A: Logs give a raw stream, not the per-step span structure.
rationale.B: Usage shows infrastructure-level metrics, not per-step execution.
rationale.C: Evaluation reports on test cases, not a live session.
rationale.D: The Traces tab inspects step-by-step execution of specific sessions, including directed acyclic graphs of spans and inputs and outputs.

stem: An airline's CX Agent Studio application must handle baggage claims, seat changes, and loyalty questions. Each domain has its own tools and policies, and product owners want to update one domain's behaviour without re-testing the others. How should you structure the application?

options.A: Three separate applications on three phone numbers, with an IVR menu asking callers to pick a domain
options.B: A root agent that invokes three specialised sub-agents, each with its own instructions and tools
options.C: One agent with every tool attached and a long instruction block divided into three labelled sections
options.D: A flow-based agent that classifies the domain with intents and then calls the matching generative agent

rationale.A: Pushes routing onto the customer and loses shared context when a caller changes topic.
rationale.B: CX Agent Studio organises applications as a root agent that orchestrates sub-agents specialised by task or domain.
rationale.C: A single large agent couples domains; any change risks regressions across all three.
rationale.D: The docs advise using LLMs, not flows, for intent classification; root-plus-sub-agents is the native pattern.

stem: An engineering director lists three needs: (1) 'always use our error-handling conventions', (2) 'when someone asks to add a payment provider, follow our 14-step integration procedure with its scripts', and (3) 'never let the agent push directly to a release branch'. Which mapping is best?

options.A: (1) a hook, (2) a subagent, (3) a rule telling the agent not to push to release branches
options.B: (1) a rule, (2) a skill with its scripts, (3) a hook that blocks the push command
options.C: (1) a plugin, (2) an MCP server, (3) a rule in AGENTS.md about release branches
options.D: (1) a skill, (2) a rule, (3) a subagent that reviews pushes before they happen

rationale.A: A hook cannot express conventions and a rule cannot guarantee the push is stopped.
rationale.B: Rules are standing instructions, skills package task-specific know-how and code, hooks intercept actions deterministically.
rationale.C: Plugins are packaging, the procedure is know-how not a tool, and rules are advisory.
rationale.D: Conventions are standing guidance, and a reviewing subagent is not a guaranteed block.

stem: A team in Singapore plans a production launch on RAG Engine and asks whether they can rely on the same launch stage as their colleagues in us-central1. What is the correct guidance?

options.A: Region choice only affects latency, never feature availability
options.B: Check the launch stage per region, since availability differs between regions
options.C: Preview regions carry the same SLA as GA regions
options.D: Launch stages are global, so any region behaves the same as us-central1

rationale.A: Feature and launch-stage differences are documented by region.
rationale.B: RAG Engine documents different launch stages by region, including allowlist GA, GA and preview regions.
rationale.C: Preview features do not carry GA service levels.
rationale.D: The documentation lists different stages per region.

stem: A compliance officer wants to express, in plain English, that an agent may look up a customer's balance but must never move money to an account added in the last 24 hours. Which capability supports this, and what is a practical limit to know?

options.A: Model Armor custom filters, limited to 4 MB of policy text
options.B: IAM conditions with CEL expressions, limited to 5,000 characters
options.C: Natural-language constraints, capped at 5,000 characters
options.D: Agent Registry endpoint descriptions, limited to 1,024 characters

rationale.A: The 4 MB figure is Model Armor's content size limit, and it does not express business rules.
rationale.B: CEL is not plain English and does not evaluate intent.
rationale.C: Natural Language Constraints let rules be written in plain English at the gateway, with a documented limit of 5,000 characters.
rationale.D: Descriptions document entries; they do not enforce rules.

stem: Analysts use a coding agent with the BigQuery remote MCP server to prototype dashboards. A review finds the agent could run DML against production tables. The analysts only need to read data and run SELECT queries. What should you change?

options.A: Grant the analysts only read and job-user roles, since the MCP server enforces their IAM
options.B: Turn on audit logs so DML statements can be reviewed after they run
options.C: Add an instruction to the agent's rules telling it to only run SELECT statements
options.D: Replace the managed server with a local MCP server that filters out DML keywords

rationale.A: The remote MCP server authorises calls with IAM, so least-privilege roles on the caller limit what the agent can do.
rationale.B: Logs are after the fact; the requirement is to prevent writes.
rationale.C: Instructions are not authorization.
rationale.D: Keyword filtering is brittle and adds unmanaged infrastructure.

stem: A CVE affects a JSON library used across 25 services. A coding agent opens upgrade PRs. Two services rely on a behaviour that changed in the patched version. Which process best balances speed and safety?

options.A: One PR per service, each gated by that service's tests and a dependency scan
options.B: Upgrade only in production images and leave source manifests on the old version
options.C: Pin the vulnerable version in the two affected services and tell the agent to skip them
options.D: One PR upgrading all 25 services at once, merged when the agent's summary says tests passed

rationale.A: Per-service changes with automated evidence surface the two behavioural breaks without blocking the other 23.
rationale.B: Diverges builds from source and hides the change from tests.
rationale.C: Leaves known vulnerabilities unaddressed.
rationale.D: Couples services and trusts the agent's word instead of CI results.

stem: A CX Agent Studio agent for an electronics retailer needs to answer questions from the product manuals stored in Cloud Storage and create support cases in ServiceNow. Which tools should you attach?

options.A: A Python code tool that downloads manuals per turn, and an OpenAPI tool for ServiceNow
options.B: A Google Search tool limited to the retailer's site, and a client function for ServiceNow
options.C: The manuals pasted into the instructions, and Integration Connectors for ServiceNow
options.D: A Cloud Storage data store tool and the ServiceNow tool

rationale.A: Reimplements retrieval badly and ignores the prebuilt ServiceNow integration.
rationale.B: Web search does not reach private manuals; a client function runs on the client, not as a server integration.
rationale.C: Manuals are far too large for instructions and would go stale.
rationale.D: CX Agent Studio provides data store tools (including Cloud Storage) and prebuilt tools for ServiceNow among its tool types.

stem: An agent that worked in staging fails in production with 'Egress request is not authorized' when calling an external API through Agent Gateway. Which two checks are most relevant? (Choose two.)

options.A: Whether an authorization policy allows this agent to reach that destination
options.B: Whether the agent identity has the roles required for gateway egress
options.C: Whether the model version used in production differs from staging
options.D: Whether the agent's session store has capacity for new sessions
options.E: Whether the destination's DNS record resolves inside the VPC

rationale.A: Agent Gateway requires an authorization policy permitting the agent-destination pair.
rationale.B: Egress authorization failures are commonly missing IAM permissions for the agent identity.
rationale.C: Model choice does not affect gateway authorization.
rationale.D: Session capacity is unrelated to egress authorization.
rationale.E: The error is an authorization decision, not a name-resolution failure.

stem: A manufacturing company's Agent Designer agent classifies maintenance requests into 12 categories. Accuracy is good for common categories but poor for three rare ones that differ by subtle wording. What is the most effective in-console change?

options.A: Remove the three rare categories and route those requests to 'Other'
options.B: Add examples contrasting the rare categories with their look-alikes
options.C: Add 'be especially careful with categories 10, 11 and 12' to the instructions
options.D: Raise the output length so the agent explains each category choice

rationale.A: Loses business information instead of improving classification.
rationale.B: Targeted contrasting examples are the in-console few-shot technique for teaching subtle distinctions.
rationale.C: Vague emphasis without examples rarely fixes a specific confusion.
rationale.D: Longer output does not change which category is chosen.

stem: Security wants a single place to declare which external APIs and services agents may reach, so that gateway policy can be applied consistently instead of each team hard-coding URLs. Which Agent Registry capability addresses this?

options.A: Storing allowed URLs in each agent's system instructions
options.B: Creating a firewall rule per destination in the agents' VPC
options.C: Registering endpoints as target destinations for central governance
options.D: Registering each team's source repository as a governed resource

rationale.A: Instructions are not enforcement and are not central.
rationale.B: Network rules cannot express agent-level policy or tool semantics.
rationale.C: Agent Registry lets you register endpoints to define target destinations, centrally governing the external APIs and services agents can connect to.
rationale.D: Repositories are not the runtime destinations policy applies to.

stem: A European insurer must choose between a proprietary SaaS model and a self-hosted open model for an agent that reads policyholder medical details. Legal has approved the SaaS provider's regional processing and data-use terms. The ML team is two people. Which factor should weigh most?

options.A: The open model's parameter count, since larger models are more secure
options.B: The SaaS model's benchmark rank, since legal approval makes costs irrelevant
options.C: Operational capacity: with legal cleared, a small team favours managed SaaS over self-hosting
options.D: Self-hosting is always required when medical data is involved, regardless of approvals

rationale.A: Size does not determine security.
rationale.B: Cost and operations still matter after legal approval.
rationale.C: Once security and residency constraints are satisfied, the cost and risk of operating models become decisive for a small team.
rationale.D: Not universally true; approved regional processing can satisfy the constraint.

stem: A platform team wants to know within minutes when an agent's quality degrades in production, not only when it errors. Which signal set is most appropriate?

options.A: Total token spend per hour
options.B: Weekly customer satisfaction survey results
options.C: Error rates, latency and sampled quality scores
options.D: CPU and memory utilisation of the agent's containers

rationale.A: Cost can stay flat while quality drops.
rationale.B: Far too slow and sparse for minutes-level detection.
rationale.C: Combining operational signals with sampled quality scoring detects degradations that never surface as errors.
rationale.D: Infrastructure health says little about answer quality.

stem: A finance stakeholder asks which dashboard shows an agent's container CPU and memory allocation alongside token usage. Where should you point them?

options.A: The Usage dashboards, which show runtime metrics and token usage
options.B: Cloud Billing reports broken down by agent name
options.C: The Traces tab, which aggregates token counts per span
options.D: The Logs tab with a query on the token field

rationale.A: Usage dashboards provide infrastructure-level metrics for the agent's runtime environment, including container CPU, memory and token usage.
rationale.B: Billing shows spend, not container allocation or token metrics per agent.
rationale.C: Traces show execution structure for individual sessions.
rationale.D: Log queries are not the dashboard for these metrics.

stem: A team wants a managed RAG pipeline over PDFs that currently sit in Cloud Storage and Google Drive, without building ingestion, chunking and embedding themselves. Which statement about RAG Engine is accurate?

options.A: It ingests from local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive
options.B: It only ingests documents that are already stored in BigQuery tables
options.C: It requires documents to be converted into embeddings before ingestion
options.D: It indexes data in place and never copies content into a corpus

rationale.A: RAG Engine accepts data from different sources, for example local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive.
rationale.B: BigQuery is not the only supported source.
rationale.C: Embedding is a stage RAG Engine performs, not a precondition.
rationale.D: Indexing creates a corpus that structures the knowledge base.

stem: A retailer built a custom connector that pushes documents from a legacy intranet into a Gemini Enterprise data store. The intranet identifies users by employee number, while the company signs in to Google Cloud through Okta with email addresses. Search results must respect intranet permissions. What should you configure?

options.A: Pure ACLs that list employee numbers, since any string is accepted as a principal
options.B: A rewrite of the intranet so that it identifies users by email before connecting it
options.C: An identity mapping store from Okta identities to employee numbers, used by the document ACLs
options.D: A public data store with a callback that filters results by employee number

rationale.A: Pure ACLs are for email-based identities recognised by Google Cloud; employee numbers need identity mapping.
rationale.B: Unnecessary; identity mapping exists for this case.
rationale.C: When external identities differ from the IdP, administrators create identity mapping stores to map IdP identities to external identities for custom connector data stores.
rationale.D: Public data stores ignore ACLs; application-side filtering is not enforcement.

stem: A security architect asks which control specifically addresses prompt-injection risks that arrive through MCP tool responses rather than through user messages. What should you name?

options.A: Model Armor screening on the gateway path, which covers MCP injection risks
options.B: Restricting the agent to read-only tools
options.C: Input validation on the user's chat message before it reaches the model
options.D: A rate limit on the MCP server to slow down attackers

rationale.A: Agent Gateway integrates Model Armor to protect against risks such as MCP prompt injection attacks.
rationale.B: Reduces blast radius but does not detect the injection.
rationale.C: The injection arrives in tool output, not the user message.
rationale.D: Throttling does not neutralise injected instructions.

stem: An architect is choosing the vector database behind RAG Engine. The team has no existing vector infrastructure, wants the fastest path to a working corpus, and may move to a higher-scale backend later. Which statement helps most?

options.A: RAG Engine has no pluggable backend; the corpus is always stored in BigQuery
options.B: Choosing a backend is irreversible once the corpus is created
options.C: RAG Engine only works with Pinecone, so an account must be created first
options.D: Several backends, including a managed default and Vector Search

rationale.A: Corpora are not stored in BigQuery by default.
rationale.B: Backends can be changed by rebuilding the corpus; nothing makes it permanent.
rationale.C: Pinecone is one of several supported backends.
rationale.D: RAG Engine supports RagManagedDb, Agent Platform Vector Search 2.0, Vector Search, Feature Store, Weaviate and Pinecone, so a team can start managed and migrate.

stem: A team wants continuous evaluation over production traffic but cannot afford to judge every conversation, and must still detect regressions in rare high-value flows. What sampling design fits?

options.A: Stratified sampling, weighted toward rare critical flows
options.B: Judging the first 100 conversations each morning
options.C: Uniform random sampling of 1% of all conversations
options.D: Judging only conversations that users rated badly

rationale.A: Stratification keeps evaluation affordable while ensuring rare but important flows are represented.
rationale.B: Time-of-day bias and no coverage guarantee for critical flows.
rationale.C: Rare critical flows may never be sampled.
rationale.D: Misses silent failures users never report.

stem: A nightly release pipeline runs the Agents CLI deployment command on a build agent with no terminal attached. The job hangs for its full 60-minute timeout waiting for a confirmation prompt nobody can answer, and the deployment never happens. What should be added to the command?

options.A: The -i / --interactive flag, so the prompt is printed to the job log
options.B: The --no-wait flag, which answers confirmation prompts automatically
options.C: A preceding agents-cli login -i step inside the pipeline
options.D: The -y / --auto-approve flag, which skips prompts and uses defaults

rationale.A: Interactive mode enables prompts, which is the cause of the hang.
rationale.B: --no-wait returns without waiting for deployment completion; it does not approve prompts.
rationale.C: login requires interactive mode and does not remove deploy prompts.
rationale.D: Non-interactive mode (-y, --auto-approve, --yes) skips prompts and is suitable for CI/CD automation.

stem: An auditor asks who did what when an agent deleted a record on a user's behalf. The company uses Agent Identity. What does the audit trail show?

options.A: Both the agent's identity and the user's identity for the action
options.B: Only the end user, since the agent acts purely as a proxy
options.C: Only the project and the API method invoked
options.D: Only the shared service account used by the agent fleet

rationale.A: When agents act on behalf of users, logs show both the agent's and the user's identities.
rationale.B: The acting agent is recorded as well.
rationale.C: Identity attribution is richer than that with agent identities.
rationale.D: Agent identities replace shared service accounts precisely to avoid this.

stem: An agent that answers HR policy questions is also given a tool that can update employee records, because 'it may be useful later'. Which principle does this violate, and what should happen?

options.A: Least privilege: remove the tool until a use case justifies it
options.B: Data minimisation: keep the tool but limit the fields it returns
options.C: Defence in depth: keep the tool but add Model Armor screening
options.D: Separation of duties: keep the tool but require a second agent to approve

rationale.A: Capabilities an agent does not need expand the blast radius of prompt injection or model error and should not be attached speculatively.
rationale.B: The risk is the write capability, not the fields read.
rationale.C: Screening content does not stop an authorised write the agent decides to make.
rationale.D: Adds cost and complexity for a capability that is not needed at all.

stem: Data engineers want their coding agent to explore BigQuery datasets, draft SQL and run it while building a new pipeline. Security requires IAM authorization and audit logs for every query, and the team does not want to run or patch any MCP server infrastructure. What should you configure?

options.A: Read-only exports of the datasets to Cloud Storage that the agent reads as files
options.B: The Google-managed remote BigQuery MCP server at its HTTPS endpoint, authorised through IAM
options.C: A custom MCP server on Cloud Run that proxies SQL to BigQuery with a single service account
options.D: A local open-source BigQuery MCP server started on each laptop with a shared service-account key

rationale.A: Loses live querying and the per-query audit trail.
rationale.B: The BigQuery remote MCP server is Google-hosted, enabled with the BigQuery API, and provides IAM authorization and audit logging.
rationale.C: Adds infrastructure to maintain and collapses every user into one identity.
rationale.D: Local servers need patching and a shared key defeats per-user IAM and audit attribution.

stem: A compliance agent must answer only from the company's approved corpus and must show which document each statement came from. Which combination of RAG Engine behaviour supports this?

options.A: Indexing rewrites the corpus into the model's weights for faithful recall
options.B: Generation uses the model's parametric knowledge and cites the corpus afterwards
options.C: Retrieval supplies relevant context and generation is grounded in it, with sources kept
options.D: Retrieval returns whole documents so the model can quote any part of them

rationale.A: Indexing builds a searchable corpus; it does not train the model.
rationale.B: Citing sources not used to produce the answer is misleading.
rationale.C: RAG Engine retrieves relevant knowledge and uses it as a guide for factually grounded responses, which is what makes citation possible.
rationale.D: Whole-document context is not required and often exceeds limits.

stem: A document-processing agent delegates a job that can take hours to a remote A2A agent. Your client should not hold a connection open, and the system must be notified when the work completes. Which A2A mechanism fits?

options.A: Server-sent events held open for the duration of the job
options.B: Polling the Agent Card until its status field changes
options.C: Synchronous request/response with a long timeout
options.D: Push notifications to a client webhook when the task updates

rationale.A: Keeping a stream open for hours is fragile and was explicitly excluded.
rationale.B: Agent Cards describe capabilities; they do not carry task status.
rationale.C: Ties up the client and often exceeds gateway timeouts.
rationale.D: A2A push notifications let the server send asynchronous updates to client webhooks, which suits long-running work.

stem: A bank standardises on ADK but some teams must use a model served outside Google Cloud for contractual reasons, while others use Gemini. The architect wants one framework and one set of patterns. Is ADK a valid choice?

options.A: Only for Java: the Python ADK is limited to Gemini models
options.B: Only through Agent Designer, which exports agents to ADK
options.C: Yes: ADK is open source and model-agnostic
options.D: No: ADK only runs Gemini models on Agent Runtime

rationale.A: Model-agnosticism is not limited to one language.
rationale.B: Unrelated; ADK is used directly in code.
rationale.C: ADK is an open-source, code-first, model-agnostic framework, so one framework can serve teams using different models.
rationale.D: ADK runs locally and on several targets and is model-agnostic.

stem: A newly installed Antigravity CLI plugin from another team introduces a hook that slows every edit. A developer wants to turn it off for a day while the owners investigate, without losing its configuration. What should they run?

options.A: agy plugin disable <name>, then agy plugin enable <name> once it is fixed
options.B: Delete hooks.json from the plugin folder by hand
options.C: /hooks to remove the hook from the running session
options.D: agy plugin uninstall <name>, then reinstall it once it is fixed

rationale.A: Plugins can be toggled with disable and enable without deletion.
rationale.B: Edits a managed package in place and may break its next update.
rationale.C: /hooks inspects active hooks; the durable toggle is disabling the plugin.
rationale.D: Uninstall removes it completely, losing local configuration.

stem: A security architect reviews how an agent's credentials are protected when its traffic passes through Agent Gateway, and asks what stops a stolen token from being replayed by another client. What does the platform provide?

options.A: DPoP-bound credentials on top of mTLS, so tokens are double-bound
options.B: Short token lifetimes of five minutes, after which replay fails
options.C: IP allow-lists on the gateway that reject unknown source addresses
options.D: Encryption of the token at rest in Secret Manager

rationale.A: When interacting through Agent Gateway, agents use Demonstrating Proof of Possession, creating double-bound credentials alongside mTLS certificates.
rationale.B: Shortening lifetimes narrows the window but does not bind the token to its holder.
rationale.C: Network filtering is coarse and fails for shared egress addresses.
rationale.D: Protects storage, not use of a token that has already been obtained.

stem: A partner runs an A2A agent on their own infrastructure. Your company's orchestrator must discover and call it under the same governance as internal agents. What is required?

options.A: Register the external agent manually in Agent Registry
options.B: Add the partner's URL to the orchestrator's prompt as a rule
options.C: Nothing: Agent Registry discovers any A2A agent reachable on the internet
options.D: Ask the partner to deploy their agent to your Agent Runtime instance

rationale.A: Agents deployed on Agent Runtime register automatically; external or third-party endpoints must be registered explicitly.
rationale.B: No governance, no discovery, no policy enforcement.
rationale.C: There is no automatic discovery of external endpoints.
rationale.D: Unnecessary and usually impossible for a partner-operated agent.

stem: A support agent's failures only appear several turns into a conversation, but the team's evaluation set contains single-turn prompts. They lack recorded multi-turn conversations. Which Agents CLI capability helps build a multi-turn evaluation set?

options.A: agents-cli eval grade, which extends single-turn cases into conversations
options.B: agents-cli eval metric list, which adds multi-turn cases for each metric
options.C: agents-cli eval dataset synthesize, which simulates users to generate multi-turn traces
options.D: agents-cli playground, which saves sessions as evaluation sets automatically

rationale.A: grade scores traces against metrics; it does not generate them.
rationale.B: It lists available metrics; it does not create cases.
rationale.C: eval dataset synthesize (experimental) synthesises evaluation traces via model-based user simulation for multi-turn conversations.
rationale.D: The playground is interactive testing; it does not synthesise datasets.

stem: An agent on Agent Runtime serves two business units whose conversation data must remain separate, and the security team wants access enforced by the platform rather than by the agent's code. Which capability should you use?

options.A: Separate Memory Bank topics per business unit
options.B: IAM Conditions on Sessions to scope access per business unit
options.C: A tag on each session, filtered by the agent before answering
options.D: Two prompts that instruct the agent to keep the units' data apart

rationale.A: Topics steer memory extraction, not access enforcement.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime Sessions support controlling access with IAM Conditions, keeping enforcement in the platform.
rationale.C: That is application-side filtering, which the team wants to avoid.
rationale.D: Instructions are not access control.
